constitution: Article XII · Mandatory Rule 1: --version/--help p95 <150ms warm / <300ms cold. Rule 2: no perf claim without a budget and a regression gate.
waiverPolicy: Any budget exceeded by a change requires a ratified waiver (docs/perf/WAIVERS.md) before merge; the regression gate fails CI otherwise.

measurement.samples: >=9 for gate runs, >=21 for baseline artifacts (cold samples use a fresh isolated XR_HOME; warm scenarios discard a warm-up sample; the single largest sample is trimmed when samples >= 15)
measurement.metric: p95 wall-clock process duration on the CI host
measurement.note: Budgets are absolute ceilings for the p95 metric (Constitution Article XII — the binding contract). doctor gate ceiling 2500ms (measured 315-474ms idle; spec target <1000ms met by measurement on the reference host) — the ceiling accommodates degraded shared runners. Raised 1500->2500 on 2026-08-12 after the audit measured doctor p95 at 1263ms (unmodified main@3308aff) and 1270ms (audit branch) on a CPU-saturated 2-vCPU host: a 0.6% delta between trees, i.e. pure host contention, yet only ~15% below the old ceiling. doctor spawns several subprocesses (commandExists/bun --version) and is the most contention-sensitive scenario in the matrix, so 1500ms was a coin-flip on a loaded runner. The measured claim (<1s on a reference host) is unchanged and still reported every run. The regression band (30% since Phase 4 · T4; was 10%) is evaluated against a SAME-HOST baseline cache (~/.cache/xr, persisted in CI via actions/cache): it blocks only when a same-host baseline exists (run 2+ on any host); otherwise it warns (run 1 seeds the cache). The band was widened from 10% after measuring same-host p95 variance up to ~±25% on the version/help micro-benches (21 samples) on shared runners — a 10% band flaked CI without a real regression; the absolute budgets above remain the binding ceilings and a ≥1.3x slowdown still fails the band. retrieval-100k budget 250ms (measured 25-42ms).
